item.title: Vertical Speaker Cut With Captions

exact_text: Today I want to show you three easy ways to make your mornings less stressful.

turns.text: Make this 9:16 with her centred and add readable English captions matching what she says. Keep the whole 10 seconds and her original voice. Put the captions below her face.

item.tests: Tests portrait reframing combined with accurate, synchronized, readable burned-in speech captions.

answer_sheet.Source and subject: Use talk-one.mp4, keeping the woman centred.
answer_sheet.Size and duration: 9:16 vertical, the full 10 seconds; free-tier resolution is fine.
answer_sheet.Caption wording and language: English: Hi everyone! Today I want to show you three easy ways to make your mornings less stressful.
answer_sheet.Caption appearance: Your call on font and styling; use readable, high-contrast captions below her face, inside the frame, in short timed chunks.
answer_sheet.Audio: Keep her original voice and sound, with no replacement narration or added music.

must_haves: The output is a 9:16 edit of the attached footage, with the woman centred and her face fully visible.
The full 10 seconds and original voice are preserved in sync.
Visible captions reproduce 'Hi everyone! Today I want to show you three easy ways to make your mornings less stressful.' in order, with no omitted or invented words.
Captions appear in short readable chunks timed to the corresponding speech rather than displaying the entire transcript throughout.
Captions have clear contrast, stay fully within the frame and do not cover her face.

turns.text: Could you edit this clip with the woman kept centred? I’m a little worried the captions might distract from her rather than help people follow along. As far as the format and timing go, make it 9:16 and keep the whole 10 seconds. Please keep her original voice, too. Add readable English captions matching what she says, and put them below her face.

dialog.agent:
For this clip, I’d use **simple white captions with a thin dark outline**, limited to two lines below her face—no bouncing words or flashy highlighting.

One limitation: the connected tools can add captions, but don’t offer a reliable crop/reframe control to make the clip **9:16 with her centred**. A generative edit could alter her appearance or original voice, so I wouldn’t use that here.

Could you upload a **centred 9:16 version**? I can then add English captions matching her speech while keeping the full 10 seconds and her original audio.
dialog.why: It asks the user to upload a centred 9:16 version and waits before adding captions. The tool limitation explains the request rather than being the final outcome.
dialog.user: The source I have is talk-one.mp4; I don’t have a separate centred 9:16 version to upload. The caption text is: “Hi everyone! Today I want to show you three easy ways to make your mornings less stressful.” Your suggested simple, high-contrast styling sounds fine, with short timed chunks below her face and inside the frame. Free-tier resolution is fine, too, and please keep her original sound without replacement narration or added music.

dialog.agent:
Thanks—the supplied caption text and styling are clear. I’ll keep the original sound, with no narration or music.

The remaining blocker is **centring her in a 9:16 frame**: the connected tools don’t provide a crop/reframe control, and a generative edit wouldn’t reliably preserve her appearance and original audio.

I can instead add simple, high-contrast English captions to the **original framing**, keeping all 10 seconds and the original sound. Would you like that caption-only version? I haven’t started a render or spent credits.
dialog.why: It asks the user to choose an alternative—adding captions in the original framing—and waits for their answer.
dialog.user: Yes, please proceed with the caption-only version in the original framing, keeping the full 10 seconds and her original sound. Please keep the captions below her face, inside the frame, in short readable chunks. I’m still a little worried about captions distracting from her, so the simple high-contrast styling you suggested sounds good.

turns.agent:
The captioning request was blocked by **insufficient Magic Hour credits**. No video was created and no credits were spent.

The intended edit remains: all 10 seconds, original framing and sound, with simple white captions, a thin black outline, and bottom-centred placement. Once credits are available, I can retry.
